title: Effect of Sintering Temperature on the Microstructure and Integrated Properties of MgAlTiVFeCo Lightweight High-Entropy Alloy

recollection.structure: guess: refined microstructure with varying grain sizes
recollection.mechanism: guess: grain growth and phase formation due to thermal energy
recollection.results: guess: improved mechanical properties such as strength and hardness at optimal sintering temperature

score.note: The recollection only identifies temperature-varied sintering, which is evident from the title, and misses SPS at 1000 °C. Its grain-size/refinement claim does not capture the dense microstructure and uniformly distributed oxide barrier phases. The thermal phase-formation mechanism is broadly plausible but omits passive-film formation, chloride blocking, and diffusion-controlled parabolic oxidation. It gives no numerical density, hardness, oxidation, or corrosion results, only a generic claim of improved hardness at an optimum temperature.
